Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 1, Verse 38

“Even if these men, their minds overpowered by greed, see no wrong in the destruction of a family and no crime in the betrayal of friends...”

Arjuna concedes that his opponents are blinded rather than wicked, which is generous of him. The concession also sets up his real argument: that seeing clearly creates an obligation.
